import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1002

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1002](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1002)
- [Ke60] Kesten, Harry, Uniform distribution {${\rm mod}\,1$}. Ann. of Math. (2) (1960), 445--471.
-/

open Real Set Filter Finset MeasureTheory Topology

namespace Erdos1002

/--
For any $0<\alpha<1$, let $f(\alpha,n)=\frac{1}{\log n}\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}(\tfrac{1}{2}-
\{ \alpha k\})$. Does $f(\alpha,n)$ have an asymptotic distribution function?

In other words, is there a non-decreasing function $g$ such that $g(-\infty)=0$, $g(\infty)=1$,
and $\lim_{n\to \infty}\lvert \{ \alpha\in (0,1): f(\alpha,n)\leq c\}\rvert=g(c)$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1002 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ g : ℝ → ℝ, Monotone g ∧
      Tendsto g atBot (𝓝 0) ∧
      Tendsto g atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      letI f :=  fun (α : ℝ) (n : ℕ) ↦
        (1 / log n) * ∑ k ∈ Icc (1 : ℕ) n, (1 / 2 - Int.fract (α * k))
      ∀ c : ℝ, Tendsto (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (volume { α | α ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ f α n ≤ c }).toReal)
        atTop (𝓝 (g c)) := by
  sorry

/--
Kesten [Ke60] proved that if $f(\alpha,\beta,n)=\frac{1}{\log n}\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}(\tfrac{1}{2}-
\{\beta+\alpha k\})$ then $f(\alpha,\beta,n)$ has asymptotic distribution function
$g(c)=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\rho c}\frac{1}{1+t^2}\mathrm{d}t$, where $\rho>0$ is an explicit
constant.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1002.variants.kesten :
    ∃ ρ > 0,
      let g := fun (c : ℝ) ↦ (1 / π) * ∫ t in Iic (ρ * c), 1 / (1 + t^2)
      ∀ c : ℝ, Tendsto (fun (n : ℕ) ↦
        (volume { p : ℝ × ℝ | let ⟨α, β⟩ := p; α ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ β ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧
          (1 / log n) * ∑ k ∈ Icc (1 : ℕ) n, (1 / 2 - Int.fract (β + α * k)) ≤ c }).toReal)
        atTop (𝓝 (g c)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1002

reformulations.difference: Relative to Erdős’s original formulation on p. 62, Lean reverses the summands’ sign and uses ≤ c instead of < c.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Reflection α ↦ 1−α preserves Lebesgue measure on (0,1), and the sum changes sign for every irrational α. Thus the two sign conventions have identical distributions. For n≥2, each level set is countable: expanding the fractional parts expresses the sum as an affine function of α plus an integer-valued sum of floors, with nonzero slope. Consequently strict and non-strict sublevel sets have equal measures. These equalities hold eventually in n, so precisely the same functions g satisfy both formulations. The full equivalence is proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean as Review1002Equiv.original_problem_iff, without sorryAx.

reformulations.difference: Lean expresses the Cauchy limit through sublevel-set measures and puts the scale in the CDF cutoff ρ*c, rather than dividing the random sum by a positive scale before asserting convergence in distribution.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing X_n for the source’s sum of fractional parts minus 1/2, normalized by log n, the standard Cauchy law is symmetric and continuous. Hence X_n/σ converges to standard Cauchy iff the CDFs of −X_n converge at every c to 1/2 + arctan(c/σ)/π. This is Lean’s integral with ρ=1/σ. Product Lebesgue measure on the unit square is the stated uniform sampling law; including its boundary changes no probabilities. Borda’s computed σ=1/(4π) corresponds to ρ=4π. The integral identity and the complete open/closed-square equivalence were checked in Lean, but not the full distributional-convergence equivalence.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, “Problems and results on diophantine approximations,” Compositio Mathematica 16 (1964), 52–65, especially p. 62, problem 3, and reference [25]: https://www.numdam.org/item/CM_1964__16__52_0.pdf

B. Borda, “Equidistribution of continued fraction convergents in SL(2,Z_m) with an application to local discrepancy,” arXiv:2303.08504v2, §§2 and 4 (the sawtooth Cauchy limit and its normalizing constant). LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2303.08504 ; publication metadata: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.08504

H. Kesten, “Uniform distribution mod 1 (II),” Acta Arithmetica 7 (1962), 355–380, introduction, equation (1.2), and references/corrections: https://www.impan.pl/shop/publication/transaction/download/product/94931

review.notes: Both declarations were checked; no mathematical defect or status discrepancy was identified. Direct access to erdosproblems.com and JSTOR’s Kesten (1960) text was blocked, so verification used Erdős’s original problem and Borda’s precise published restatement of Kesten’s result. Lean checks confirmed measurability, finite sublevel-set measures (≤1), harmless values at n=0,1, and integrability of the Cauchy kernel. All experiments are under /workspace/review; no checkout files were edited.
